NICHEROVER analyses for females and males

data_iso <- readRDS("../data/data_iso.rds")

col4PCA <- c('MasterID','MainID','Trip','Sex','ProcedureYear','d13C',   'd15N', 
             'StandardLength_cm','ProcedureDate')  


PCAdata <- data_iso[,col4PCA] 
PCAdata$ProcedureYear <- as.factor(PCAdata$ProcedureYear)
m.PCAdata <- dplyr::filter(PCAdata, Sex == "Male") # Extract the data just for males , 48 males
m.PCAdata <- dplyr::filter(m.PCAdata, Trip == "PostBreeding") # Extract the data just for PB males , 23 males
m.PCAdata$MasterID <- paste(substring(m.PCAdata$MasterID, 1, 6),substring(m.PCAdata$MasterID, 16, 19),sep='') # Shorten the IDs for the plot
rownames(m.PCAdata) <- m.PCAdata[,1] # Assign row names

Analysis for Male PB NESE

row.names(m.PCAdata) <- m.PCAdata$MasterID


#First exploratory PCA with all data, including Isotopes
m.PCAdata.1 <- na.omit(m.PCAdata)

m.PCAdata.1.1 <- as.data.frame(scale(m.PCAdata.1[c(6:8)]))

# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
hc.m.all <- hclust(dist(m.PCAdata.1.1, method = "euclidean"), method ="ward.D2")
hc.m.all
## 
## Call:
## hclust(d = dist(m.PCAdata.1.1, method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
## 
## Cluster method   : ward.D2 
## Distance         : euclidean 
## Number of objects: 13
plot(hc.m.all, hang = -0.01, cex = 0.7)

# Check how many clusters there are 
res.nbclust <- NbClust(m.PCAdata.1.1, distance = "euclidean",
                       min.nc = 2, max.nc = 10, 
                       method = "ward.D2", index ="alllong")
## Warning in pf(beale, pp, df2): NaNs produced
## Warning in pf(beale, pp, df2): NaNs produced

## *** : The Hubert index is a graphical method of determining the number of clusters.
##                 In the plot of Hubert index, we seek a significant knee that corresponds to a 
##                 significant increase of the value of the measure i.e the significant peak in Hubert
##                 index second differences plot. 
## 

## *** : The D index is a graphical method of determining the number of clusters. 
##                 In the plot of D index, we seek a significant knee (the significant peak in Dindex
##                 second differences plot) that corresponds to a significant increase of the value of
##                 the measure. 
##  
## ******************************************************************* 
## * Among all indices:                                                
## * 6 proposed 2 as the best number of clusters 
## * 8 proposed 3 as the best number of clusters 
## * 1 proposed 4 as the best number of clusters 
## * 1 proposed 5 as the best number of clusters 
## * 3 proposed 8 as the best number of clusters 
## * 2 proposed 9 as the best number of clusters 
## * 6 proposed 10 as the best number of clusters 
## 
##                    ***** Conclusion *****                            
##  
## * According to the majority rule, the best number of clusters is  3 
##  
##  
## *******************************************************************
# Agree that 3 is the correct number of clusters
# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
fit <- cutree(hc.m.all, k = 3)
plot(hc.m.all)
rect.hclust(hc.m.all, k=3, border="red")

# Add the Cluster to the original table
m.PCAdata.1$IntClusters <-  paste('Cluster',cutree(hc.m.all, k =3))


f <- fviz_dend(hc.m.all, 
               k =3,
               cex = 0.6,                     # Label size
               palette = "jco",               # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
               rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE, # Add rectangle around groups
               rect_border = "jco",           # Rectangle color
               labels_track_height = 0.8,      # Augment the room for labels
               main = "Cluster analysis for PB Males")

Niche Analysis

d <- 3
Psi <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(d^2), d, d)) # scale

m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters <-  paste('Cluster',cutree(hc.m.all, k =3))
aggregate(m.PCAdata.1.1[1:3], m.PCAdata.1.1[4], mean)
##   IntClusters       d13C       d15N StandardLength_cm
## 1   Cluster 1 -0.7472564 -0.5592584        -1.2493247
## 2   Cluster 2 -0.9869292 -1.0533605         0.8671783
## 3   Cluster 3  0.7432224  0.6911224         0.1637770
# Generate parameter draws
nsamples <- 1e4
system.time({
 PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.1), m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters,
                    function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.1[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))
})
##    user  system elapsed 
##    2.68    0.19    3.38
# various parameter plots
clrs <- c("#e41a1c",
          "#377eb8",
          "#4daf4a",
          "#984ea3",
          "#ff7f00") # colors for each cluster

legend("topleft", legend = names(PM.par), fill = clrs)
dev.off()

niche.par.plot(PM.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = FALSE, plot.Sigma = TRUE)

# 2-d projections of 50 niche regions
nsamples <- 50
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.1), m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.1[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# format data for plotting function
PM.data <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.1), m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters, function(ii) X = m.PCAdata.1.1[ii,1:3])

pdf("../figures/NicheRegionsMalesPB.pdf")
niche.plot(niche.par = PM.par, niche.data = PM.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c(expression(paste(delta^{13}, "C")),expression(paste(delta^{15}, "N")),
                        'Standard Length'), col = clrs, xlab = expression("Variables"))
dev.off()
## png 
##   2
niche.plot(niche.par = PM.par, niche.data = PM.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c(expression(paste(delta^{13}, "C")),expression(paste(delta^{15}, "N")),
                        'Standard Length'), col = clrs, xlab = expression("Variables"))

#########################

# niche overlap plots for 95% niche region sizes
nsamples <- 10000
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.1), m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.1[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# Overlap calculation.  use nsamples = nprob = 10000 (1e4) for higher accuracy.
# the variable over.stat can be supplied directly to the overlap.plot function

over.stat.PM <- overlap(PM.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))

#The mean overlap metrics calculated across iterations for both niche 
#region sizes (alpha = .95 and alpha = .99) can be calculated and displayed in an array.
over.mean.PM <- apply(over.stat.PM, c(1:2,4), mean)*100
round(over.mean.PM, 2)
## , , alpha = 95%
## 
##            Species B
## Species A   Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
##   Cluster 1        NA      6.53      3.10
##   Cluster 2      6.21        NA     15.62
##   Cluster 3      1.87     12.39        NA
## 
## , , alpha = 99%
## 
##            Species B
## Species A   Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
##   Cluster 1        NA     12.34      8.35
##   Cluster 2     11.34        NA     28.23
##   Cluster 3      3.51     20.81        NA
# Credibility Intervals
over.cred.PM <- apply(over.stat.PM*100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(over.cred.PM[,,,1]) # display alpha = .95 niche region
## , , Species B = Cluster 1
## 
##        Species A
##         Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
##   2.5%         NA         0         0
##   97.5%        NA        46        15
## 
## , , Species B = Cluster 2
## 
##        Species A
##         Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
##   2.5%          0        NA         0
##   97.5%        47        NA        56
## 
## , , Species B = Cluster 3
## 
##        Species A
##         Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
##   2.5%          0         0        NA
##   97.5%        30        62        NA
# Overlap plot
#clrs <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3") # colors for each cluster
over.stat.PM <- overlap(PM.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = .95)
pdf("../figures/NicheOverlapMalesPB.pdf")
overlap.plot(over.stat.PM, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = "Males Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")
dev.off()
## png 
##   2
overlap.plot(over.stat.PM, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = "Males Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")

###############################   Niche Size   #################################

# posterior distribution of (mu, Sigma) for each strategy
nsamples <- 10000
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.1), m.PCAdata.1.1$IntClusters,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.1[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# posterior distribution of niche size by species using the 75% contour to define strategy niche
PM.size <- sapply(PM.par, function(spec) {
  apply(spec$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = .75)
})

# point estimate and standard error
rbind(est = colMeans(PM.size),
      se = apply(PM.size, 2, sd))
##     Cluster 1 Cluster 2 Cluster 3
## est  18.06761  16.71302 16.182473
## se   14.63688  15.39342  7.940378
# Niche Size
PM.size2 <- matrix(NA, nrow = 30000, ncol = 2)
colnames(PM.size2) <- c("Niche_Size", "SubCluster")
PM.size2[1:10000,1] <- PM.size[,1]
PM.size2[1:10000,2] <- 'SubCluster 1'
PM.size2[10001:20000,1] <- PM.size[,2]
PM.size2[10001:20000,2] <- 'SubCluster 2'
PM.size2[20001:30000,1] <- PM.size[,3]
PM.size2[20001:30000,2] <- 'SubCluster 3'

PM.size2 <- as.data.frame(PM.size2)
PM.size2$Niche_Size <- as.numeric(PM.size2$Niche_Size)

# Bhattacharyya coefficient to see how different the niche sizes are
# Create an empty matrix

Olap.PM <- matrix(NA,3,3)
colnames(Olap.PM) <- c('SubCluster 1',
                        'SubCluster 2',
                        'SubCluster 3')

rownames(Olap.PM) <- c('SubCluster 1',
                        'SubCluster 2',
                        'SubCluster 3')

for (sc in 1:3){
  for (sc2 in 1:3){
    Olap.PM[sc,sc2] <-  bhatt.coeff(PM.size[,sc], PM.size[,sc2])
  }
  
}

Olap.PM
